skill.name: project-setup-architecture
skill.description: Set up React Native and Expo project infrastructure with TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle, Zustand, testing, linting, and a feature-focused folder structure.
skill.summary: Guide React Native and Expo project setup across core tooling, architecture, data, state, and verification steps.
skill.author: BabakBar

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, visible setup commands, documentation links, and a sample local SQLite filename. No prompt injection, malicious intent, credential access, exfiltration, or hidden network behavior was found in SKILL.md. Because the workflow includes package and migration commands, users should still review commands before execution.

remediation.issue: Package manager and migration commands may be executed in user projects.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands are examples and should be reviewed before execution, especially package-name placeholders and migration steps.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples trigger automated security detections.
remediation.suggestion: Separate command examples from agent instructions, and label them as optional setup snippets where practical.

content.value_statement: Starting an Expo app requires many setup choices across tooling, database, state, and tests. This skill gives practical setup steps for a consistent React Native foundation.
actual_capabilities: Guides TypeScript setup for React Native and Expo projects.
Provides a feature-focused source directory structure.
Shows SQLite and Drizzle setup with a local database client.
Includes a simple Zustand store pattern for shared state.
Lists Jest, Testing Library, ESLint, and Prettier setup steps.
Provides a verification checklist for compile, test, lint, and app checks.
limitations: It is a setup guide, not a full project generator.
Examples assume a React Native and Expo codebase.
Package versions must be checked against the project Expo SDK.
It does not cover CI, deployment, authentication, or secret management.

use_cases.title: Start a New Expo App
use_cases.description: Create a practical setup path for TypeScript, folders, database, state, tests, linting, and formatting.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Structure
use_cases.description: Use the suggested folders and setup checklist to align a team on a predictable app foundation.

use_cases.title: Add Missing Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Introduce database, state management, testing, or linting to an existing Expo app in focused steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a step-by-step setup plan for a new Expo React Native app with TypeScript and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Core Tooling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to help configure TypeScript, linting, formatting, and the recommended source folders for my Expo project.

prompt_templates.title: Add Data and State Layers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add SQLite, Drizzle, migrations, and a small Zustand store to my existing Expo project.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare my current Expo project structure with the recommended setup and identify practical changes.

output_examples.input: Set up a new Expo project with TypeScript, testing, and linting.
output: A staged setup checklist covering TypeScript, dependencies, folders, test tooling, linting, formatting, and verification.
Notes about which commands should be reviewed before running in the project.

output_examples.input: Add persistence and state management to an existing app.
output: A focused plan for adding SQLite, Drizzle, migrations, and a shared state store.
Validation steps for database access, state updates, tests, and type checking.

output_examples.input: Review whether my app structure is ready for feature development.
output: A gap list for folders, configuration files, package scripts, and verification checks.
A recommended order for making changes with minimal disruption.

best_practices: Install and verify one infrastructure layer at a time.
Use Expo-compatible installation steps for Expo packages.
Run type checks, tests, linting, and app startup checks after setup changes.
anti_patterns: Installing many packages before confirming SDK compatibility.
Mixing database, state, navigation, and test changes in one unverified step.
Copying placeholder package names or app identifiers without project review.

faq.question: What type of project is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is designed for React Native projects that use Expo.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete app?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance, examples, and verification steps for core infrastructure.

faq.question: Can I use it with an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the relevant sections to add missing tooling or review your current structure.

faq.question: Does it choose exact package versions?
faq.answer: No. Check package versions against your Expo SDK and project constraints.

faq.question: Does it cover backend services?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on local app infrastructure such as TypeScript, SQLite, state, tests, and linting.

faq.question: Should commands run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review setup commands before execution, especially dependency and migration commands.
